survey: A stylized saguaro cactus on a sand dune. Main trunk: a tall ribbed column with a rounded top, standing upright. It sits in a shallow hollow in the sand, so it clearly rests on the ground rather than floating. Left arm: grows out of the trunk's left side at mid-height, curves out and up, and ends in a rounded ribbed tip. Its elbow joins the trunk smoothly, with no gap and no overlap. Right arm: grows out of the trunk's right-front side a little higher up, bends upward and ends in a rounded tip. The joint is a thick, believable fleshy connection. Spines are small yellow points spread along the ribs of the trunk and both arms. A single pink flower with a green bud base sits at the crown of the trunk, which is where real saguaros bloom. Pebbles lie on the sand around the base. The view is a slight three-quarter angle. Two arms, one trunk and one flower are a plausible count, and each part attaches where a real cactus would.
